items.title: A finite CW complex has the edge-and-2-cell presentation
items.design_state: Locally authored A-page prerequisite or intermediate result required by the assigned finite-group BF proof route; complete statement and proof are recorded on the owning page.
items.statement: Let $K$ be a finite connected CW complex, let $v_0$ be a vertex, and let $T$ be a maximal tree in its 1-skeleton. Choose one orientation of each 1-cell outside $T$. For each such edge $e:u\to v$, let $x_e$ be the based loop that follows $T$ from $v_0$ to $u$, traverses $e$, and returns along $T$ from $v$ to $v_0$. For every 2-cell $f$, choose a point on its attaching circle and a path in the 1-skeleton from $v_0$ to its image; the resulting based attaching loop has a unique reduced word $r_f$ in the free basis $(x_e)$. Then

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Chapter 1, §1.2 Applications to Cell Complexes and §1.A Graphs and Free Groups
references.locator: Proposition 1.26, PDF pp. 49–51, for attaching 2-cells and higher cells; Proposition 1A.2, PDF pp. 83–85, for the maximal-tree basis.

items.strategy: 1.1 The 1-skeleton of a connected CW complex is connected: attaching a cell of dimension at least two has connected attaching sphere, so it cannot join two components of the preceding skeleton. Since $K$ is finite, its 1-skeleton is a finite connected graph. The unique paths in $T$ contract it to $v_0$, supplying the contraction required by [F2]. The quotient that collapses $T$ to a point is a wedge with one circle for each 1-cell outside $T$, and [F3] gives the free basis represented by the loops $x_e$. [given, F2, F3, construct]

items.title: Piecewise-smooth paths and thin homotopies
items.design_state: Step 1 local prerequisite expansion; complete statement and proof authored before consumers.
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and $U\subseteq M$ open. A **piecewise-smooth path** in $U$ is a continuous map $\gamma:[0,1]\to U$ for which some finite partition $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_n=1$ makes every restriction $\gamma|_{[t_{j-1},t_j]}$ smooth as a map of manifolds with boundary. Its source and target are $\gamma(0)$ and $\gamma(1)$. The collection of all such paths is a set: it is a subset, defined by separation, of the function set from $[0,1]$ to $U$.

Two paths $\gamma_0,\gamma_1$ with the same source $x$ and target $y$ are **thin-homotopic**, written $\gamma_0\sim_{\mathrm{thin}}\gamma_1$, if there is a continuous map $H:[0,1]^2\to U$ and a finite subdivision of the square into compact curvilinear triangles such that $H$ is smooth up to each triangle's boundary, $H(0,t)=\gamma_0(t)$, $H(1,t)=\gamma_1(t)$, $H(s,0)=x$, $H(s,1)=y$, and $\operatorname{rank}(dH_{(s,t)})\le 1$ on every smooth triangle. A **curvilinear triangle** here is a compact region $D$ equipped with a specified homeomorphism $\psi:\Delta^2\to D$ from the standard closed two-simplex which is a smooth embedding on the interior, extends smoothly to a neighborhood of $\Delta^2$ in its affine span, and maps the three edges of $\Delta^2$ to the three boundary arcs of $D$. Saying $H$ is smooth up to $D$'s boundary means that $H\circ\psi$ extends smoothly from $\Delta^2$ to an open neighborhood of $\Delta^2$ in its affine span, with values in $U$; equivalently, it is a smooth singular $2$-simplex under the neighborhood-extension convention of [[def-smooth-singular-simplex]]. The rank is the dimension of the image of the differential from the two-dimensional tangent space of the triangle to $T_{H(s,t)}M$, computed through the interior chart $\psi$ and extended to boundary points by these smooth extensions. The quotient by this relation is used only after its equivalence and compatibility properties are proved.

references.title: Urs Schreiber and Konrad Waldorf, Parallel Transport and Functors, §2.1, Definitions 2.1–2.2

items.title: Thin path classes form a groupoid
items.design_state: Step 1 local prerequisite expansion; complete statement and proof authored before consumers.
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and $U\subseteq M$ open. For composable piecewise-smooth paths $\gamma:x\to y$ and $\delta:y\to z$ in $U$, define $\delta*\gamma:[0,1]\to U$ by $(\delta*\gamma)(t)=\gamma(2t)$ for $0\le t\le\tfrac12$ and $(\delta*\gamma)(t)=\delta(2t-1)$ for $\tfrac12\le t\le1$. Thus $\delta*\gamma$ traverses $\gamma$ first and then $\delta$. A groupoid means a category in which every morphism is an isomorphism.

Then thin homotopy is an equivalence relation on each set of piecewise-smooth paths with fixed endpoints, and concatenation respects the equivalence classes. Tag a morphism by its endpoints and its path class. With objects the points of $U$, morphisms $x\to y$ the tagged classes $[\gamma]$ from $x$ to $y$, composition $[\delta]\circ[\gamma]=[\delta*\gamma]$, identity the class of the constant path, and inverse $[\gamma]^{-1}=[\bar\gamma]$ where $\bar\gamma(t)=\gamma(1-t)$, the resulting category is a groupoid.

references.title: Urs Schreiber and Konrad Waldorf, Parallel Transport and Functors, §2.1, Definition 2.2 and Lemma 2.3

items.title: Thin path groupoid
items.design_state: Step 1 local prerequisite expansion; complete statement and proof authored before consumers.
items.statement: A **groupoid** is a category in which every morphism has a two-sided inverse. For an open subset $U$ of a smooth manifold, the **thin path groupoid** $\Pi^{\mathrm{thin}}_1(U)$ is the category whose objects are the points of $U$ and whose morphisms from $x$ to $y$ are tagged triples $(x,y,[\gamma])$, where $[\gamma]$ is a thin-homotopy class of piecewise-smooth paths from $x$ to $y$; composition, identities, and inverses are those of Proposition [[prop-gr-fx-thin-path-quotient-groupoid]].

references.title: Urs Schreiber and Konrad Waldorf, Parallel Transport and Functors, §2.1, Definition 2.4

items.title: The once-around circle path is not thin-contractible
items.design_state: Step 1 local prerequisite expansion; complete statement and proof authored before consumers.
items.statement: Let $S^1=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2=1\}$ with its regular-level-set smooth structure. For $\gamma(t)=(\cos(2\pi t),\sin(2\pi t))$, $0\le t\le1$, the morphism $[\gamma]$ in $\Pi^{\mathrm{thin}}_1(S^1)$ is not the identity morphism at $(1,0)$.

references.title: Urs Schreiber and Konrad Waldorf, Parallel Transport and Functors, §2.1

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of transport along a piecewise-smooth path
items.design_state: Step 1 local prerequisite expansion; complete statement and proof authored before consumers.
items.statement: Let $n\ge1$ and let $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_m=1$ be a finite partition. For each $j$, let $A_j:[t_{j-1},t_j]\to M_n(\mathbb R)$ be continuous. There is a unique continuous function $U:[0,1]\to M_n(\mathbb R)$ that is $C^1$ on each partition interval, satisfies $U'(t)=-A_j(t)U(t)$ in its interior, and has $U(0)=I_n$. Derivatives at interval endpoints are the corresponding one-sided derivatives.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §3.3 Parallel transport
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, Chapter 3

items.title: Connection path transport
items.design_state: Planned claim authored with complete local argument or exact well-defined definition.
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, $U\subseteq M$ a nonempty open set with a smooth tetrad, and $\omega$ its Lorentz-connection matrix from [[def-gr-fx-tetrad-spin-connection]]. Assume the supplier's $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention. For a piecewise-smooth path $\gamma:[0,1]\to U$, let $A_\gamma(t)=\omega_{\gamma(t)}(\dot\gamma(t))$ on each smooth piece. By Proposition [[prop-gr-fx-connection-path-transport-exists]], there is a unique continuous piecewise-$C^1$ solution

$$\dot U_\gamma(t)=-A_\gamma(t)U_\gamma(t),\qquad U_\gamma(0)=I_4.$$

The endpoint matrix $U_\gamma(1)$ is the **connection path transport** in the chosen tetrad trivialization. It maps vector components at $\gamma(0)$ to components at $\gamma(1)$ under the convention of the supplier. A smooth local Lorentz frame change transforms this matrix by its endpoint frame matrices; it is a gauge transformation in the principal-bundle sense only if it extends to an automorphism over the identity as in [[def-gauge-group-of-a-smooth-principal-bundle]].

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §3.3 Parallel transport
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, Chapter 3

items.title: Connection transport is invariant under thin homotopy
items.design_state: Step 1 local prerequisite expansion; complete statement and proof authored before consumers.
items.statement: Under the assumptions of [[def-gr-fx-connection-path-transport]], if two piecewise-smooth paths $\gamma_0,\gamma_1:[0,1]\to U$ are thin-homotopic in the sense of [[def-gr-fx-thin-paths]], then $U_{\gamma_0}(1)=U_{\gamma_1}(1)$ in the fixed tetrad trivialization.

references.title: Urs Schreiber and Konrad Waldorf, Parallel Transport and Functors, arXiv:0705.0452, §2.1 and Appendix B.3
David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §3.3.3

items.title: Path transport composes and transforms covariantly
items.design_state: Planned claim authored with complete local argument or exact well-defined definition.
items.statement:
For transport as in [[def-gr-fx-connection-path-transport]], with composition convention $[\delta]\circ[\gamma]=[\delta*\gamma]$ meaning first traverse $\gamma$ and then $\delta$,

$$U_{\delta*\gamma}(1)=U_\delta(1)U_\gamma(1),\qquad U_{\bar\gamma}(1)=U_\gamma(1)^{-1}.$$

Let $E=(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ be the tetrad of [[def-gr-fx-connection-path-transport]]. For each $x\in U$, let $E_x:\mathbb R^4\to T_xM$ send the standard basis vector $\mathbf e_I$ to $E_I(x)$; because the tetrad vectors are a basis, $E_x$ is an invertible real-linear map, hence a linear isomorphism ([[def-linear-isomorphism-and-invertible-linear-map]]). A groupoid is a category in which every morphism is an isomorphism ([[def-isomorphism-groupoid-and-connected-category]]). Define the target groupoid $\mathcal T(U)$ to have base-point-tagged objects $\tau_x:=(x,T_xM)$ for $x\in U$ and morphisms $\tau_x\to\tau_y$ the tagged triples $(\tau_x,\tau_y,L)$ where $L:T_xM\to T_yM$ is a real-linear isomorphism; identities and composition are tagged identity maps and ordinary composition ([[def-category]]). A covariant functor assigns objects and morphisms and preserves identities and composition ([[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]]). The functor from the thin path groupoid [[def-gr-fx-thin-path-groupoid]] to $\mathcal T(U)$ sends $x$ to $\tau_x$ and sends $[\gamma]:x\to y$ to the tagged tangent-space arrow

$$\bigl(\tau_x,\tau_y,E_y\,U_\gamma(1)\,E_x^{-1}\bigr):\tau_x\longrightarrow\tau_y.$$

Here $U_\gamma(1)$ acts on tetrad components, while $E_y$ and $E_x^{-1}$ convert between components and tangent vectors. Under the supplier convention $e'=\Lambda e$, the component matrix in the changed local frame satisfies

$$U'_{\gamma}(1)=\Lambda(\gamma(1))U_\gamma(1)\Lambda(\gamma(0))^{-1}.$$

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§3.3–3.4.2
Urs Schreiber and Konrad Waldorf, Parallel Transport and Functors, arXiv:0705.0452, §2.1

items.title: Small-loop transport recovers curvature
items.design_state: Planned claim authored with complete local argument or exact well-defined definition.
items.statement:
Fix coordinate dimension $n\ge2$ and matrix size $q\ge1$, independently. Let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be an open coordinate domain, let $K\subset V$ be compact with positive distance from $\mathbb R^n\setminus V$, and let $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ be the standard basis of $\mathbb R^n$. Let $\omega=\sum_{k=1}^n\omega_k(x)\,dx^k$ be a $C^2$ $M_q(\mathbb R)$-valued connection one-form, with each $\omega_k:V\to M_q(\mathbb R)$. Along each segment use the matrix ODE $U'=-\omega(\dot\gamma)U$ and initial value $I_q$; existence and uniqueness for this fixed matrix size follow from [[prop-gr-fx-connection-path-transport-exists]]. For the tetrad connection of [[def-gr-fx-connection-path-transport]], take $q=4$. For $p\in K$, distinct coordinate directions $i,j$, and sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$ so the square stays in $V$, define $\gamma_\varepsilon$ by traversing each straight side at constant speed over one quarter of $[0,1]$, in the order

$$p\to p+\varepsilon e_i\to p+\varepsilon e_i+\varepsilon e_j\to p+\varepsilon e_j\to p.$$

Its boundary orientation is positive for the ordered coordinate pair $(e_i,e_j)$.

$$U_{\gamma_\varepsilon}(1)=I_q-\varepsilon^2F_{ij}(p)+O(\varepsilon^3),\qquad F_{ij}=\partial_i\omega_j-\partial_j\omega_i+[\omega_i,\omega_j]\in M_q(\mathbb R).$$

Here $I_q$ is the identity in $M_q(\mathbb R)$ and fix a norm $\|\cdot\|$ on that space satisfying $\|AB\|\le\|A\|\,\|B\|$ for all $A,B\in M_q(\mathbb R)$. The notation $O(\varepsilon^3)$ means that the norm of the remainder is at most $C\varepsilon^3$ for all sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$, with $C$ uniform for basepoints $p\in K$.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §3.3.3 and §3.4.2
S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, Chapter 3

items.title: SU(2) is a compact Hausdorff matrix group
items.design_state: Step 1 local prerequisite expansion; complete statement and proof authored before consumers.
items.statement:
Let $M_2(\mathbb C)$ have its Euclidean topology as $\mathbb R^8$, write $Q^\dagger:=\overline Q^{\mathsf T}$ for conjugate transpose, and define

$$SU(2)=\{Q\in M_2(\mathbb C):Q^\dagger Q=I_2,\ \det Q=1\}.$$

Under matrix multiplication, $SU(2)$ is a compact Hausdorff topological group.

references.title: Emmanuel Kowalski, An Introduction to the Representation Theory of Groups (2025), §5.2
John C. Baez, Spin Network States in Gauge Theory, arXiv:gr-qc/9411007, §2

items.title: Finite SU(2) graph holonomy model
items.design_state: Planned claim authored with complete local argument or exact well-defined definition.
items.statement:
A **finite oriented graph** consists of finite vertex and edge sets $V,E$, source and target maps $s,t:E\to V$, and a fixed-point-free involution $e\mapsto\bar e$ with $s(\bar e)=t(e)$ and $t(\bar e)=s(e)$. A **finite SU(2) graph configuration** assigns $g_e\in SU(2)$ to every oriented edge and requires $g_{\bar e}=g_e^{-1}$. A graph path is a finite composable edge word $e_1,\ldots,e_n$; its holonomy is the later-left product $g_{e_n}\cdots g_{e_1}$, and the empty path has holonomy $I_2$.

A vertex gauge assignment is a function $h:V\to SU(2)$. It acts on edge variables by

$$g_e\longmapsto g'_e=h_{t(e)}g_eh_{s(e)}^{-1}.$$

A **finite-dimensional unitary representation** is a group homomorphism $\rho:SU(2)\to U(W)$ on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $W$ that is strongly continuous, meaning $g\mapsto\rho(g)w$ is continuous for each $w\in W$. Here

$$U(W):=\{T\in\operatorname{GL}(W):\langle Tv,Tw\rangle=\langle v,w\rangle\text{ for all }v,w\in W\},$$

with the operator-norm topology inherited from $\operatorname{End}(W)$. In finite dimension, strong continuity is equivalent to continuity in this operator norm.

For a closed graph path $\ell=(e_1,\ldots,e_n)$, the associated **Wilson trace** is the basis-independent trace of the endomorphism of $W$ given by

$$\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\rho(g_{e_n})\cdots\rho(g_{e_1})\bigr).$$

Here the trace of a finite-dimensional endomorphism is the trace of its matrix in any basis.

references.title: John C. Baez, Spin Network States in Gauge Theory, arXiv:gr-qc/9411007, §2
Emmanuel Kowalski, An Introduction to the Representation Theory of Groups (2025), §§2–3

items.title: Wilson traces are invariant under vertex gauge transformations
items.design_state: Step 1 local prerequisite expansion; complete statement and proof authored before consumers.
items.statement: For every finite SU(2) graph configuration, continuous finite-dimensional unitary representation $\rho$, closed graph path $\ell$, and vertex gauge assignment $h$, the Wilson trace of $\ell$ is unchanged by $g_e\mapsto h_{t(e)}g_eh_{s(e)}^{-1}$.

references.title: John C. Baez, Spin Network States in Gauge Theory, arXiv:gr-qc/9411007, §2
Emmanuel Kowalski, An Introduction to the Representation Theory of Groups (2025), §§2–3

items.title: Finite graph vertex Haar averaging is an orthogonal projection
items.design_state: Planned claim authored with complete local argument or exact well-defined definition.
items.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let a finite oriented graph be given, fix total orders on its finite vertex and edge sets, and for each edge $e$ choose a finite-dimensional strongly continuous unitary representation $\rho_e:SU(2)\to U(V_e)$. At a vertex $v$ set

$$W_v=\bigotimes_{t(e)=v}V_e\;\otimes\!\bigotimes_{s(e)=v}V_e^*,$$

where the edge order induces the order on each factor list and an empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$. Use the dual action $g\cdot\lambda=\lambda\circ\rho_e(g^{-1})$ on $V_e^*$, with the dual Hilbert inner product determined by any orthonormal basis of $V_e$. On elementary tensors use the tensor-product inner product $\langle\bigotimes_i u_i,\bigotimes_i w_i\rangle=\prod_i\langle u_i,w_i\rangle$, extended sesquilinearly. Let $R_v$ be the resulting diagonal unitary representation and define its fixed-vector subspace by

$$W_v^{SU(2)}:=\{w\in W_v:R_v(g)w=w\text{ for every }g\in SU(2)\}.$$

An orthogonal projection onto a subspace $S\subseteq W_v$, regarded as an endomorphism of $W_v$, is the idempotent with range $S$ and kernel $S^\perp$.

For the normalized Haar probability measure $\mu$ on $SU(2)$,

$$P_vw:=\int_{SU(2)}R_v(g)w\,d\mu(g)$$

is the orthogonal projection of $W_v$ onto its invariant subspace $W_v^{SU(2)}$. The vector integral is defined coordinatewise in the finite-dimensional space, equivalently by the weak integral in [[def-haar-averaging-operator-on-hom-spaces]]. On the coefficient space $W=\bigotimes_{v\in V}W_v$, with vertex order fixed as above, the operators $P_v$ acting on their respective vertex factors commute, and $\prod_{v\in V}P_v$ projects onto the tensors invariant at every vertex. This is a finite kinematic projection; it imposes no Hamiltonian or continuum constraint.

references.title: John C. Baez, Spin Network States in Gauge Theory, arXiv:gr-qc/9411007, §2
Emmanuel Kowalski, An Introduction to the Representation Theory of Groups (2025), §§5.2.1 and 5.2.11

title: Holonomy and discrete geometric interfaces — Examples

items.title: Holonomy and discrete geometric interfaces — flat local transport with global holonomy
items.design_state: Planned claim authored with complete local argument or exact well-defined definition.
items.statement:
Let $M=S^1\times\mathbb R^3$, write $(x,y)$ for the standard embedding coordinates on $S^1$, and set $\alpha=x\,dy-y\,dx$. With real coordinates $t,z_1,z_2$ on $\mathbb R^3$, define

$$g=-dt\otimes dt+\alpha\otimes\alpha+dz_1\otimes dz_1+dz_2\otimes dz_2.$$

The global frame $E_0=\partial_t$, $E_1=-y\partial_x+x\partial_y$, $E_2=\partial_{z_1}$, $E_3=\partial_{z_2}$ is an orthonormal tetrad for $g$ with signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Here $E_1$ is the restriction of the indicated ambient vector field to $S^1$, where it is tangent because it is orthogonal to $(x,y)$. Orient $M$ by this ordered frame and time-orient it by $E_0$. Let $J$ be the constant matrix with $JE_2=E_3$, $JE_3=-E_2$, and $JE_0=JE_1=0$. Assume the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention in [[def-gr-fx-tetrad-spin-connection]]. Define $\omega=\tfrac14J\alpha$ and the affine connection on this frame by

$$\nabla_X\Bigl(\sum_Jv^J E_J\Bigr):=\sum_I\Bigl(X(v^I)+\sum_J\omega^I{}_J(X)v^J\Bigr)E_I.$$

For a real $4\times4$ matrix $A$, $\exp(A)$ denotes the matrix series $\sum_{m=0}^\infty A^m/m!$, which converges absolutely in any fixed submultiplicative matrix norm.

This is a flat Lorentz connection. On any coordinate arc of $S^1$ with angular coordinate $\theta$, transport between endpoints is $\exp(-\tfrac14J(\theta_1-\theta_0))$, independent of the chosen path inside that arc. Around the once-around loop it is $\exp(-\tfrac\pi2J)\ne I_4$, although the curvature is zero; the loop is not thin-contractible.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§3.3.3–3.4.2
Urs Schreiber and Konrad Waldorf, Parallel Transport and Functors, arXiv:0705.0452, §2.1

items.title: Holonomy and discrete geometric interfaces — triangular graph Wilson trace
items.design_state: Planned claim authored with complete local argument or exact well-defined definition.
items.statement: Take the oriented triangle $v_0\xrightarrow{e_1}v_1\xrightarrow{e_2}v_2\xrightarrow{e_3}v_0$, assign $g_{e_1}=g_{e_2}=g_{e_3}=I_2$, and use the defining representation $\rho:SU(2)\to U(\mathbb C^2)$ given by $\rho(g)v:=gv$ for column vectors $v\in\mathbb C^2$. Let $k=\operatorname{diag}(i,-i)\in SU(2)$ and take the vertex gauge assignment $h_{v_0}=k$, $h_{v_1}=h_{v_2}=I_2$. The first and third edge matrices change to $k^{-1}$ and $k$, respectively, while the loop product remains $I_2$ and its Wilson trace remains $2$.

references.title: John C. Baez, Spin Network States in Gauge Theory, arXiv:gr-qc/9411007, §2
Emmanuel Kowalski, An Introduction to the Representation Theory of Groups (2025), §§2–3

items.title: Holonomy and discrete geometric interfaces — antisymmetric SU(2) intertwiner
items.design_state: Planned claim authored with complete local argument or exact well-defined definition.
items.statement:
At a vertex with two incoming edges carrying the defining representation $\rho(g)v:=gv$ for $g\in SU(2)$ and $v\in V=\mathbb C^2$, the vertex space is $W_v=V\otimes V$. For a basis $e_1,e_2$ of $V$, the nonzero antisymmetric tensor

$$\epsilon=e_1\otimes e_2-e_2\otimes e_1$$

is invariant under the diagonal action $g\otimes g$. Consequently the normalized Haar projection $P_v$ of [[prop-gr-fx-vertex-haar-projection]] fixes it: $P_v\epsilon=\epsilon$.

references.title: John C. Baez, Spin Network States in Gauge Theory, arXiv:gr-qc/9411007, §2
Emmanuel Kowalski, An Introduction to the Representation Theory of Groups (2025), §§2–3 and §5.2
